reproduction.text: Lays eggs, 7 to 20 at a time

overview.text: The Coastal Taipan is an extremely venomous snake of northern and eastern Australia and New Guinea. It is the second-longest venomous snake in Australia, after the King Brown Snake.

identification.text: Light olive or reddish-brown above and paler below.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Averages about 2 m and 3 kg; the longest reach about 2.9 m.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Coastal northern and eastern Australia - from north-western Western Australia across the Northern Territory and Queensland into northern New South Wales - and southern New Guinea.

behaviour.text: Mostly active by day, especially in the early to mid morning, but may hunt at night in hot weather. It usually avoids people, but becomes very defensive if provoked.

diet.text: Mostly rats, mice and bandicoots, and sometimes birds.

reproduction.text: Breeds between August and December and lays 7 to 20 eggs, which hatch after 60 to 80 days. The babies are 30 to 34 cm long and grow fast - about 1 m in their first year.

funfacts.text: Baby taipans grow about 6.7 cm a month - reaching about 1 m in their first year.

recognise.text: Long, slender, plain olive or reddish-brown snake.
